question: When can a diffusion model's reverse score be computed from a bounded spatial neighborhood, can locality be characterized as a phase property of data distributions, and where along a noise path must a global denoiser be used?

key_findings.claim: Exponential decay of spatial conditional mutual information is sufficient for approximate local Bayes reversal of a local forward-noise channel.
key_findings.evidence: For a tripartition A-B-C, the paper constructs a Bayes recovery channel using only the AB marginal. A classical Fawzi-Renner inequality bounds its KL error, and hence squared total variation error, by I(X_A:X_C|X_B). In the infinitesimal diffusion limit, the resulting reverse drift uses the local marginal score d/dx_A log P_AB.

key_findings.claim: The multiple-step construction yields an explicit receptive-field scaling with Markov length, system size, number of steps, and target error.
key_findings.evidence: After decomposing each forward step into local channels, the reordered recovery construction gives total variation error below epsilon when the buffer radius satisfies r_n at least on the order of xi_n log(NK/epsilon). The authors state that the factor N may be a proof artifact, so this is a sufficient upper bound rather than a matching locality lower bound.

anchors.section: III.C Local reversibility of multiple-step denoisers

key_findings.claim: The proposed data-phase equivalence is existential and bidirectional: two distributions share a phase if some local forward path admits a local reverse process that stays near the same path.
key_findings.evidence: Section III.D requires a local or quasi-local Fokker-Planck evolution from P_0 to Q_0 and a local denoising evolution back to P_0, with both endpoint and pathwise total-variation error at most epsilon. Because only one such path must exist, whether a particular Gaussian-noise path crosses a nonlocal transition is not itself a phase invariant.

anchors.section: III.D Phases of data distributions, Equation (9)
VII Discussion, path dependence and liquid-vapor analogy
Supplement S4, bypassing a pathwise transition

key_findings.claim: On MNIST and Fashion-MNIST, an estimated conditional-mutual-information barrier appears around normalized noise time 0.3-0.4, while both clean data and near-white-noise endpoints look spatially Markovian.
key_findings.evidence: MINE estimates I(X_A:X_C|X_B) for a center pixel and varying buffer width under linear alpha_t=t corruption. The curves are low at t=0 and t=1 but remain large across distances near t approximately 0.3-0.4; noncentral-pixel and Fashion-MNIST replications are qualitatively similar. Ordinary two-pixel mutual information decays monotonically and does not reveal this barrier.

anchors.section: V Numerical Results, Figure 3 and Equation (11)
Supplement S2.E, CMI versus two-point information

key_findings.claim: Local-denoiser failure tracks the estimated CMI barrier, and a time-gated hybrid uses global U-Nets only in the transition window without visible degradation in the displayed MNIST samples.
key_findings.evidence: Modified U-Nets with limited receptive radii fail to reconstruct recognizable samples once corruption extends beyond roughly 0.4, with smaller radii failing slightly earlier. In the 64-sample comparison, radius-3 denoisers outside [0.2,0.5] plus global denoisers inside that interval look comparable to all-global generation; swapping the allocation makes many digits unrecognizable.

anchors.section: Supplement S3.B, denoiser architecture and scan

key_findings.claim: The quantum-to-classical correspondence is constructive but is not needed for the empirical local-denoiser result.
key_findings.evidence: The paper derives classical diffusion and score-based reversal as the fully decohered limit of Lindblad dynamics and continuous-time twirled Petz recovery. This motivates the phase definition and proof organization, while the classical Bayes recovery bound on page 4 already establishes the core local-score sufficiency claim independently.

anchors.section: VI Relation to phases of mixed states

key_findings.claim: The experiments do not yet establish a computational or sample-efficiency win, nor do they prove that global networks are necessary at the observed window.
key_findings.evidence: The evidence is confined to 28-by-28 MNIST variants, qualitative 64-image panels, neural lower-bound estimates of mutual information, and separately trained local/global U-Nets. No FID, likelihood, wall-clock, FLOP, parameter, or training-data comparison is reported. The theorem proves locality when CMI decays but does not provide the converse lower bound that high estimated CMI forces every bounded network to fail.

method.core_idea: Treat spatial conditional independence as an operational certificate that a globally defined diffusion score can be replaced by a marginal score on a finite neighborhood, then define data phases by mutual local recoverability along a diffusion path.
method.mechanism: The theory combines classical Bayes recovery, a conditional-mutual-information recovery inequality, and a reorganization of local channels over multiple time steps. Empirically, MINE estimates spatial CMI along a linear noise path, and receptive-field-limited U-Nets test whether local reversal succeeds in the same time regions.
assumptions: Data live on a spatial lattice with meaningful bounded neighborhoods.
All relevant tripartitions have exponentially decaying CMI away from a transition.
The forward diffusion decomposes into bounded local channels and the accumulated approximation-error bound is usable.
Neural mutual-information estimation preserves the qualitative time-and-distance structure of true CMI.
MNIST and Fashion-MNIST phase behavior is informative about larger real-world spatial datasets.

techniques.role: Constructs an exact global reverse channel and its AB-marginal local approximation.
Certifies approximate spatial Markovianity and bounds local recovery error.
Controls accumulated recovery error across local channels and diffusion steps.
Estimates spatial conditional mutual information from image samples.
Empirically probes the spatial radius required at each noise time.
Uses global computation near the diagnosed transition and local computation elsewhere.

evaluations.setting: MNIST under pixelwise linear Gaussian interpolation from clean data at t=0 to noise at t=1
evaluations.metric: MINE estimate of I(X_A:X_C|X_B) versus buffer distance and time
evaluations.result: Low endpoint values and a distance-persistent barrier around t=0.3-0.4, reproduced at noncentral pixels
evaluations.baseline: Pairwise pixel mutual information, which decreases monotonically and does not show the barrier

evaluations.setting: Flow-matching recovery of partially corrupted MNIST with U-Nets restricted to radius r
evaluations.metric: Qualitative recognizability across corruption endpoint T_f and receptive radius
evaluations.result: All tested local denoisers degrade strongly beyond about T_f=0.4; smaller radii fail somewhat earlier

evaluations.setting: Full MNIST generation with radius-3 and global denoisers assigned to complementary time windows
evaluations.result: Global only in [0.2,0.5] appears comparable to all-global; global only outside that interval produces many unrecognizable digits

evaluations.metric: CMI heatmaps and local-denoiser output panels
evaluations.result: A similar 0.3-0.4 barrier and post-transition local-denoiser failure are reported

limitations: The locality theorem is sufficient, not a matching necessity theorem for high CMI or global network size.
MINE is a neural lower-bound estimator and may confound estimator capacity or optimization with true Markov length.
Evaluation is limited to small grayscale 28-by-28 datasets and qualitative generation panels.
The proposed efficiency benefit is not measured in FLOPs, latency, memory, parameters, or sample complexity.
Separate local models across radii or intervals may offset savings that a single deployable architecture would realize.
The transition and best global-compute window can depend on the chosen noise path and schedule.
failure_modes: A local denoiser loses global semantic coherence when Markov length approaches image size.
A noisy CMI estimator can allocate expensive global computation to the wrong timesteps.
A fixed receptive field fails earlier as resolution or dependency length grows.
Patchwise scores can create locally plausible but globally inconsistent mosaics.
A hybrid system may introduce discontinuities or calibration mismatch when switching between local and global score estimators.
reusable_insights: Measure denoiser receptive-field sensitivity across time before assigning uniform model capacity to every diffusion step.
Conditional rather than pairwise mutual information is the relevant diagnostic for information that bypasses a spatial buffer.
Noise-path design can be treated as an optimization problem over maximum recovery length, not only signal-to-noise ratio.
A deployable hybrid should jointly learn a locality gate and nested receptive fields, then account for gate overhead in end-to-end compute.
open_questions: Can lower bounds show that large Markov length requires nonlocal score computation under a specified approximation class?
Do the CMI barrier and hybrid-compute benefit persist on ImageNet-scale pixels, latents, video, or text-conditioned generation?
Can cheap score-Jacobian or attention diagnostics replace the expensive MINE sweep online?
Can evolutionary or differentiable search find noise paths and schedules that minimize peak recovery length while preserving likelihood and sample quality?
How should one train a single nested architecture whose receptive field changes smoothly with diffusion time?

competitive_landscape.title: Patch Diffusion: Faster and More Data-Efficient Training of Diffusion Models
competitive_landscape.difference: Randomizes patch size and conditions on patch coordinates to obtain measured training speedups and FID results; it does not diagnose a time-local phase boundary or prove recovery from spatial CMI.

competitive_landscape.title: An analytic theory of creativity in convolutional diffusion models
competitive_landscape.relationship: Competing theory of local convolutional scores
competitive_landscape.difference: Builds analytic local and equivariant-local score machines that predict trained convolutional denoisers and explains patch-mosaic creativity; the present paper instead uses recoverability and CMI to decide when locality should fail.

competitive_landscape.title: A Phase Transition in Diffusion Models Reveals the Hierarchical Nature of Data
competitive_landscape.difference: Studies a high-level feature-reconstruction transition in hierarchical data and validates on class-unconditional ImageNet; the present work defines a spatial-recovery transition and tests local receptive fields on MNIST variants.

competitive_landscape.title: Efficient and Training-Free Single-Image Diffusion Models
competitive_landscape.difference: Computes tractable multiscale patch scores for a single reference image and reports megapixel/gigapixel generation speed; it operationalizes training-free locality in a narrower single-image setting without the phase/CMI framework.

competitive_landscape.title: Towards a Mechanistic Explanation of Diffusion Model Generalization
competitive_landscape.difference: Investigates how architectural locality changes memorization/generalization behavior, whereas the present paper focuses on a recovery-length certificate and time-varying network scope.

novelty_assessment.author_claim: Spatial Markov length supplies an operational definition of data phases, a proof of when diffusion denoisers may be local, and a principle for concentrating global network capacity near a narrow phase-transition window.
novelty_assessment.evidence: The Bayes-recovery bound and multi-step construction establish the sufficiency result; CMI sweeps, receptive-field failures, and the time-gated MNIST panel align on a similar transition interval.
novelty_assessment.reviewer_inference: The distinctive contribution is connecting recovery-theoretic phase language to adaptive denoiser locality. The system claim remains preliminary because necessity, large-scale quality, and realized compute savings are not demonstrated.
